newsitem.title: PERU: Six die in Peru snowstorm, thousand feared trapped.
newsitem.headline: Six die in Peru snowstorm, thousand feared trapped.

text.p: At least six people, including three infants, have died in a vicious snowstorm that has trapped about a thousand people inside their vehicles on a highway in Peru's Andes, Civil Defence officials said on Sunday.

Transport companies reported about 40 vehicles, including 12 passenger buses -- each carrying more than 50 people -- have been stuck since Friday when the storm began, regional Civil Defence head Luis Barra told Reuters.
The vehicles were trapped on a 50-mile (80-kilometre) highway between Abancay and Puquio, 375 miles (600 km) southeast of Lima, he added.

A group of soldiers, who reached the trapped vehicles on foot early on Sunday, reported by portable radio that six people had died in their vehicles, Andres Salazar, acting head of Peru's Civil Defence, told Reuters.

Civil defence officials also set out later on Sunday to walk through the five-foot (1.5-metre) deep snow in temperatures about 14 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 10 degrees Centigrade) to take blankets and provisions to those trapped, Barra said. But the ongoing storm has prevented access to the vehicles by air or road, he added.
"The fear is that if the storm keeps up, there will be more deaths," Barra said. "There has never before been snow like this here."
A destructive weather phenomenon, known as El Nino, which hits Peru every two to seven years, has begun to form off the Pacific coast resulting in unusually cold temperatures to the Andes.
